correctness.rationale: The endpoint benchmark holds with or without a positive ordinary path: the 0–m conductance is x+1/H with H=Σ1/a_i, or just x if the path is broken. It is at most x+Σa_i/m² by Cauchy–Schwarz. At c≥m² the bound is attained by the uniform open path; for c>m² endpoint equality forces x=0 and uniform saturated a_i. At c=m² a missing ordinary edge could tie the endpoint bound only if all ordinary conductances were zero, which disconnects the graph for m≥2. Otherwise equality forces uniform y. Independently, the grounded path Laplacian with ordinary weights y has inverse entries min(i,j)/y, and the closing edge adds x e_m e_m^T. The rank-one inverse formula gives R_k=k/y - x(k/y)^2/(1+xm/y); comparison to R_m gives (m-k)(kx/y-1)≤0. This yields exactly x∈[0,B/(m(2m-1))]. For c<m² the uniform open path perturbed by small x lowers R_m while all other pairs retain a strict gap, so no open path can be optimal. Connected support gives continuous pair resistances by a grounded inverse; a cut whose summed conductance tends to zero gives divergent cross-cut resistance by the unit-voltage energy bound. This proves the needed lower semicontinuity and existence. Normalize all saturated optimizers to the critical simplex. For ε=m²-c the rescaled objective there is (1-εx/B)Δ. Comparing the upper endpoint to the constant lower bound m²/B forces normalized x≥x_* and Δ→m²/B. Compactness and the critical classification then force every normalized limit to be the same upper endpoint; the rescaling tends to one. As an exact check at m=3,B=1, the critical endpoint has R_1=6, R_2=R_3=9; at c=8, x=1/15 and y=7/45 give Δ=135/16<9. Read the frozen result, audit, review, verification note, metadata, slogan and rational arc verifier without executing it. The proof and grounded inverse above give the all-parameter replay, not the packaged finite count. Below threshold this checks retention and the limit, not a closed optimizer formula or uniqueness.

value.rationale: Worst-pair resistance is a natural robust design objective. The useful part is not just the simple sufficient price bound; it is the complete degenerate segment and proof that every sequence of optimal designs approaching from below selects its positive endpoint. That distinction matters when using a critical-cost optimum as a limit of perturbations and is not provided by a finite solver run.
